# WP-08 inventory: Prolix

Written before any code, per the extend-ACs-before-code rule, and after the Molt lesson: every entry below was **read**, not sized.

## STOP FIRST: a live production credential is committed to this repository

**`scripts/flysql:15` contains a plaintext password for the `geodica-db` cluster**, together with the cluster address and user. It is not Prolix-scoped: the script's own `DB_MAP` opens `conflab_prod`, `laksa_prod` and `prolix_prod`, so the credential reaches **three production databases across three projects**.

It is in git history, so deleting the file does not remove it -- `git log -S` finds it in two commits, `f21484b` ("Add flysql script for geodica-db MPG access") and `5f78f3b`. **Rotation is the only fix that fixes anything, and it is hv's call entirely.**

**hv's ruling, 2026-08-10: proceed as if rotated.** Every affected repository is private; several unrelated private projects share this managed PG instance, and hv will rotate them all on one day, after this work lands, so that the change is single and coordinated rather than piecemeal. hv's own words: *"it is (very) bad practice, I know, and so I will fix it. Just not now."* Recorded as a deliberate, informed deferral rather than an oversight.

This is not a devbin finding and this WP does not resolve it. It is recorded here because the migration would otherwise have **copied the credential into a new file** -- a `bin/.devbin/cmd/` handler or a `config.yaml` `run:` line -- which turns one exposure into two and puts a fresh timestamp on it. **One rule survives the ruling, and it is the reason this section stays at the top: the credential is MOVED, never COPIED.** Porting `flysql` means `git mv` into its handler, not transcribing it. A copy would put the same secret in a second file with a fresh timestamp and make rotation day a hunt instead of a one-file edit. Deleting the script is still not this WP's call either -- deletion without rotation removes nothing, since git history holds it regardless.

## What this WP is, versus what its brief said

**Prolix is a `scripts/` MIGRATION, not the fresh install the brief describes.** It has no `bin/` directory at all and a twelve-entry, 235-line `scripts/` fleet. This is the same staleness that hit WP-02 and WP-03 (mis-sized, harmless) and WP-05 (destructive). Corrected before starting, not at close.

The brief's `Dependencies` line also reads "The elixir protocol (WP-01) and, softly, everything before it". **WP-01 is cancelled.** The elixir protocol was in fact proven at WP-02, WP-03 and WP-04, all of which are done, so the dependency is satisfied by different work than it names.

Confirmed as briefed, and still true: `native/ios/Prolix.xcodeproj` exists, `Dockerfile` and `fly.toml` exist, and there is no root `.tool-versions`.

**What is NOT true any more: Prolix is no longer "last on top of a by-then boring elixir path".** It is the only WP left in the thread. Molt was to have proven the shell shape ahead of it and is cancelled, so `shell` and `swift` gate scope both reach this WP unexercised, on the project that also carries the first live deploy-image arm.

## `REPL_MODE` is LIVE here, and the arca_cli precedent does not transfer

At arca_cli, `REPL_MODE` was dropped, and not as a judgement call -- that project's own `dead_code_gate_test.exs` asserts zero sites for it. **Prolix is the opposite.** `lib/prolix/application.ex:27-36` and `:101-108` branch on it to choose console versus file logging, and `lib/prolix/cli.ex:74` sets it. It is load-bearing.

So the `REPL_MODE=true` prefix in `scripts/cli` and `scripts/iex` **is carried**, not dropped. Reusing arca_cli's disposition here would have silently removed working behaviour -- the same shape of error as reusing a stale caller survey, and the reason a per-project inventory is not a formality.

One thing to establish at equivalence rather than assert now: `lib/prolix/cli.ex:74` sets `REPL_MODE` itself, so the prefix may be redundant for `cli` while remaining load-bearing for `iex -S mix`, which runs no task. **Probe it; do not reason about it.**

## Dispositions -- all twelve entries

| entry          | lines | what it does                                                        | disposition                                                                        |
| -------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cli`          | 7     | `REPL_MODE=true mix prolix.cli $*`                                  | builtin `cli` via `project.cli_task: prolix.cli` -- REPL_MODE carried               |
| `iex`          | 3     | `REPL_MODE=true iex -S mix $*`                                      | builtin `iex` -- REPL_MODE carried; runs no task, so the prefix is load-bearing     |
| `repl`         | 36    | rlwrap + `mix prolix.cli repl`                                      | builtin `repl` + `cli_task`; completions data moves (arca_cli precedent)            |
| `completions/` | (423B)| static rlwrap completion list                                       | data moves to `bin/completions/repl.txt`; nothing generates it                      |
| `server`       | 3     | `LAKSA_CONFIG_* mix phx.server $*`                                  | builtin `server`; the env prefix is DEAD, see below                                 |
| `test`         | 3     | `LAKSA_CONFIG_* mix test --trace $*`                                | `test mix`; `--trace` is a deliberate delta to record, env prefix dropped           |
| `mix`          | 3     | `LAKSA_CONFIG_* mix $*`                                             | **not ported** -- with the dead prefix removed this is bare `mix`, wrapping nothing |
| `mcduct`       | 1     | clean + deps.update + compile + test                                | **DELETE, do not port** -- hv's standing disposition, 2026-08-10                    |
| `echo`         | 15    | runs `./scripts/mix run scripts/echo_task.exs`                      | **BROKEN -- bin unported**, see below                                              |
| `taillog`      | 40    | tails `.<dirname>/logs/<YYYYMMDD>.log`                              | candidate `bin/.devbin/cmd/` handler; genuinely useful, no builtin equivalent       |
| `dbproxy`      | 2     | `fly proxy 5433:5433 --app prolix-db`                               | one-line `run:` in config, or a handler beside `taillog`                            |
| `flysql`       | 126   | interactive/one-shot SQL against three prod DBs via `fly ssh`       | port by `git mv` into a handler -- **moved, never copied**; see the top of this file |

### `scripts/echo` has been broken for some time

It ends `./scripts/mix run scripts/echo_task.exs`. **`echo_task.exs` does not exist** -- not in `scripts/`, not anywhere in the repository outside `deps/` and `_build/`. The script cannot have worked since that file went away. It is binned unported, and the finding is that nobody noticed, which is the same story as arca_cli's `update_completions` and Multiplyer's dead SIA pipeline: an unexercised path stays green by never being run.

### `LAKSA_CONFIG_PATH` / `LAKSA_CONFIG_FILE` are dead, and they name the wrong project

Three scripts -- `mix`, `server`, `test` -- prefix their command with `LAKSA_CONFIG_PATH=. LAKSA_CONFIG_FILE=config.json`. They are copy-paste from Laksa, a different project in the same fleet.

> **CORRECTED AT EQUIVALENCE, 2026-08-10. The conclusion below held; the reason first written here did not, and the reason is what generalises.**
>
> This section originally read "**Prolix reads neither variable**: nothing under `lib/`, `config/` or `test/` mentions `LAKSA_CONFIG`." That is false. `config/.env` mentions both, on lines 2 and 3, in a file that is TRACKED and loaded by `config/runtime.exs:13` in dev and test. The original search missed it.
>
> The true reason is a layer down. `arca_config` resolves `<DOMAIN>_CONFIG_PATH` where the domain is `Application.get_env(:arca_config, :config_domain)`, and this project sets `config_domain: :prolix` (`config/config.exs:187`, again at `lib/prolix/application.ex:18`). So the live names are `PROLIX_CONFIG_PATH` / `PROLIX_CONFIG_FILE` -- exactly what `lib/prolix/config.ex:38-40` documents. Checked by name: `LAKSA_CONFIG_PATH`, `LAKSA_MAILERSEND_TOKEN` and `LAKSA_MAILERSEND_INUSE` are all read by nothing.
>
> **And the consequence differs from arca_config's, which is why the reason mattered.** There the dead setting lived only in the scripts, so deleting them removed it. Here it is ALSO in the committed `.env`, so deleting `scripts/` does not remove it: it stays, in a tracked file, named for a different project. A grep that had found `.env` would have said so at inventory time instead of at equivalence.

Dropped, with the reason recorded, exactly as arca_config's `ARCA_CONFIG_PATH=.arca` was. This is the third project in this thread whose `scripts/` carried an environment prefix that did nothing, and the second where the prefix belonged to a different project. **Ask what the target already does before porting what the source did** -- and ask whether the source did anything at all.

Removing the prefix is also what empties `scripts/mix`: with it gone the script is `mix $*`, a wrapper around nothing.

## Naming and config, settled from the survey

- **`project.cli_task: prolix.cli`** -- the module is `Mix.Tasks.Prolix.Cli` (`lib/mix/tasks/prolix_cli.ex:1`), so the name-derived `prolix_cli.cli` would be wrong, exactly as at arca_cli. Read by both `cli` and `repl`.
- **`commands.build.enabled: false`** -- `mix.exs` declares no escript, so there is nothing to build. This follows arca_config, not arca_cli (where an escript is genuinely declared).
- **Launcher name is `bin/prolix`, and there is no collision** -- `bin/` does not exist. The Molt hazard does not arise here; it was checked rather than assumed. Alias is hv's to name.

## Open for hv

1. ~~**The `flysql` credential.** Rotate, and separately decide what happens to the script.~~ **Ruled 2026-08-10: proceed as if rotated; hv rotates all sharing projects together, later.** The move-not-copy rule stands.
2. **`flysql`'s home even after rotation.** It queries conflab, laksa and prolix. It is a personal multi-project ops tool that happens to live in one project's repository, which is a Highlander question this thread cannot settle alone.
3. **The alias** for `bin/prolix` (`px`? none?).
4. **`.tool-versions`**: add at the fleet pins per the standing policy, which is what the policy says, but this project has never had one.

## As built, 2026-08-10 -- devbin is in, and what the first sealed baseline found

Five commits at Prolix: fence `312c3d3`, deps `2abecde`, Oban `5408034`, install + config (`81de3fa` and its predecessor), lockfile tidy `f6826e5`. Prolix ST0028 raised for what is left.

**The fence was proven, not assumed**, because this project's hook is the raw-prettier shape. A deliberately misformatted probe `.md` under `bin/.devbin/lib/` came back rewritten with no fence and byte-identical with it, while a project `.md` staged beside it was still formatted normally. The second half is the one that matters: a fence that stopped the project's own Markdown being formatted would be a regression dressed as a fix. It then held through the real install commit -- `help.md` at `123bf23` either side, manifest intact.

**Installed `--lang elixir` only, deliberately.** Prolix has Swift at `native/ios` and its intent config declares shell too, but the catalogue's swift rows have never met a real project. Arming them is AC-08.3's own step with its own evidence rather than a passenger on the install.

**The baseline could not be taken before the update, and that is the honest record.** Prolix would not compile on Elixir 1.20.3 at all, so no sealed baseline existed to take -- the same unobtainable-baseline shape that retired AC-01.4 unmet at Multiplyer, except this project could be fixed. So the first seal is a POST-update reading, and it is red on three arms:

| arm       | seal `20260810-1818` | finding                                        | disposition          |
| --------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| COMPILE   | 1572 bytes           | 11 warnings under `--warnings-as-errors`       | Prolix ST0028        |
| DEPS      | 438 bytes            | 23 lockfile entries nothing requires           | FIXED here, `f6826e5`|
| TOOLCHAIN | 141 bytes            | no `.tool-versions` at all                     | Prolix ST0028        |

`check deps` is green at `20260810-1819` after `mix deps.unlock --unused`, suite unchanged. Two of the 23 orphans, `tesla` and `hackney`, were on the morning's advisory list purely as dead lockfile weight -- never resolved, so never a real exposure.

**`test all` reports FAILED and the suite is GREEN, which is the seal doctrine working.** The MIX seal is 0 bytes at 746 passed; the CREDO arm is red at 228 findings. hv ran it independently at `20260810-1821` and got a character-identical result -- the seals differ in byte size only because a tty adds ANSI colour. Credo is recorded red and sized separately, as at arca_cli.

## A Highlander crack in devbin's own base, found here

`check critic` scanned **shell, elixir and swift** while `config.yaml` declares elixir only. It reads `intent/.config/config.json` directly (`lib/cmd/check:31`); everything else in devbin reads `project.languages` via `lib/resolve:61`. **Two sources for one fact.** It did not bite -- nothing was staged, so the arm examined nothing either way -- but a project whose two files disagree gets a critic run its gate scope never asked for. To be filed as a devbin issue, not patched from here.
